newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday due to increasing demand for funds by financial institutions before the Chinese Lunar New Year in early February, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.52 percent from 10.20 percent last Friday.
Total turnover rose to 9.36 million lots from 7.78 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"More financial institutions borrowed money today to cover liquidity shortages before the Lunar New Year," said one trader. "This has become the key factor for repurchase trading."
Trading on the repo market is usually dominated by the fund requirements of institutions for speculation on the stock markets, traders said.
But around the Lunar New Year, it is often overshadowed by the need to cover a shortfall in funds to settle the year's accounts, they said.

Traders said the trend is likely to continue until around mid-February although the stock market movements will continue to be an important factor. "The rates are likely to move up in the short term due to the increasing demand," a second trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up with funds flowing in from the weak domestic share markets.
The most active three-year bond that matures in September 1999 rose slightly to 102.31 yuan from 102.25 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market increased to 782,090 lots from 517,168. The one-year bill issued early last year matured today and stopped trading.

"The sharp losses on the A share markets today drove much liquidity to the spot market," one trader said. "If the A share markets continue to be weak in the next few trading days, the spot contracts will rise further."
